To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the New Zealand state sector is in a state of flux, and that this flux has been generated in part by the paradoxes inherent in the thermostatic metaphor.
the performance management systems in place in the New Zealand state sector are a complex mixture of the thermostatic metaphor and the pendulum swing metaphor.

(1) performance management is a paradoxical phenomenon; (2) the paradoxical nature of performance management is not a problem to be overcome, but rather an opportunity for learning; (3) performance management is best conceptualized as a ‘pendulum swing’; (4) the pendulum swings between two poles — the ‘control’ pole and the ‘empowerment’ pole — and (5) the pendulum is currently swinging towards empowerment.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the extent to which the new performance management regime has achieved the desired balance between control and autonomy, and whether the balance has been achieved in a way that is consistent with the principles of New Public Management.
the nature, causes and consequences of the ‘pendulum swings’ between the imperatives of control and purpose in New Zealand's public sector.
the paradoxes of performance management, and with how they are being resolved through pendulum swings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
New Zealand is now seeking a more balanced approach between control and empowerment.
the New Zealand reforms are an example of a swing of the pendulum in the opposite direction, and that the reforms are a reaction to the perceived excesses of the previous pendulum swing.

the reforms have been successful in achieving a new balance between central and local government, between central government agencies and the control agencies and between central government and local authorities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pendulum has swung too far in the direction of control.
the pendulum has swung back and forth between the poles of centralisation and decentralisation, between the poles of control and autonomy, between the poles, in short, of ‘command’ and ‘empowerment’.
performance management has not been the panacea that was promised for New Zealand’s public sector.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance management reforms have not produced the expected outcomes.
there are no simple solutions to the problems of performance management, and that there are no universal solutions.
there is no simple solution, but that the pendulum can be moved in a more productive direction.
